newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks close lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks close lower on profit-taking.

text.p: SPI Futures 2623.0 -12.0 US 30yr cl 6.90 -0.02
10yrbond futs 92.655 +0.045 Gold NY 343.50 Lon fix 343.90
AUD US$0.7598 (Mon $0.7582) CRB Index cl 248.64 -2.32
*Stocks give up Monday's gains on profit-taking and a fall on Wall Steet, but still near highs. Volume 367.71 million, A$1.04 billion, 1,158 stocks traded, 335 steady, 383 up, 440 down.
Profit-taking and a fall on Wall Street saw Australian stocks pull back on Tuesday, giving up most of Monday's gains, but the market remains near its highs.
The All Ordinaries Index ended down 12.1 points at 2,613.6, near its lows for the day after a short-lived rally towards positive territory around the midsession.
"There's been some profit-taking in this market," said Shaw Stockbroking dealer Jamie Spiteri.
"The noticeable falls were in the resources sector...and the broader market was easier."
The June share price index futures contract ended down 12 points at 2,623, maintaining a 9.4 point premium to the physical market.

Dealers said the market had taken some of its early tone from Monday's fall on Wall Street, while investors were keen to take profits after a rally which has seen the All Ords gain more than 80 points in the past two-and-half weeks.
The All Resources Index declined 0.94 percent, with Australia's biggest company the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd falling 28 cents to A$18.87.
Among other major miners, Rio Tinto Ltd was down 23 cents at A$21.12 and WMC Ltd down 15.3 cents at A$8.18.
Westpac Banking Corp headed the turnover table, easing 20 cents to A$6.92 after going ex-dividend 19 cents with 9.3 million shares changing hands.
The other banks were mixed, with ANZ Ltd easing 13 cents to A$9.12 after Monday's strong rise in the wake of better than expected first half profits.
Overall, falls outnumbered gains seven to six, while traders said turnover of A$1.04 billion belied a fairly quiet day.
Macquarie Bank Ltd leaped to a new high, jumping 50 cents to A$10.00, following Monday's stronger than expected annual profits.
Rural services group Iama Ltd rose seven cents to A$2.93 after reporting a nine percent rise in interim net profits, despite difficult trading conditions and dry weather.
Most market sectors recorded declines on the day, although property trusts remained in the black.
"They've got an underlying support level in a low interest rate environment," said a Sydney-based dealer.
Fosters Brewing Group ended steady on turnover of 5.9 million shares following renewed speculation about a possible A$2.5 billion share buy-back.
In other markets, the Australian dollar found some support, trading at US$0.7597 by 5.00 p.m. (0700 GMT), from US$0.7582 late on Monday, but most dealers remain bearish.
Long-dated Australian bond yields extended a recent rally in anticipation of a moderate first quarter GDP figure on Wednesday, with 10-year bonds at 92.645, up 0.035.
